brief: Verdict ahead of the print: Tydal credit support and funding, not mining.
Kona: Tydal's $202/kW-month from a smaller tenant shows the price of weak credit and how LCs try to cover it.
changes: Report date: 10 November, before the 8:00 a.m. ET call.
AI backlog rose to $2.9bn from $0.9bn in September; ARR about $86mn.
$100mn buyback on 8 October alongside a $1bn ATM filed 10 August.
A102 moved from 4Q26 to 1Q27 without explanation; infrastructure updates move to quarterly.
B. Riley cut its target to $19 and Barclays raised to $17 in October.
checks: Built before results. Date from the company announcement. 2Q, Tydal terms and ATM from SEC filings, checked by a fresh subagent; corrections applied (group margin, gross vs IT MW, 30 June commitments, named LC bank). Revenue consensus single undated aggregator; labelled Provisional. Price from MarketBeat on 3 November, article internally inconsistent. Ortex and short interest not reopened. No bond or convert quote.
consensus_thesis: Investors own Bitdeer for the conversion of owned power into contracted AI revenue with mining cash flow alongside, and avoid it for losses, dilution and unleased capacity; at about $6.76 on 3 November (about $1.56bn, near a 52-week low) and about 26% of float short, the market doubts funding and tenant credit at Tydal. Provisional: limited preview material; no convert or bond price found.
headline: 3Q26 revenue (consensus about $247.7mn, single aggregator) matters less than whether the Tydal letters of credit and project debt are in place before the first delivery in 4Q26, and how much of the $1bn ATM funds the gap.
kona: Tydal shows how far rent rises for a weaker tenant: about $202/kW-month over 16 years, with a year-10 exit and $1.3bn of letters of credit doing the work a stronger tenant's rating would. If the LCs close, that is a structure Kona could copy; if they do not, it shows high rent without credit support cannot be financed. Tydal's rent is also well above the US peer rents on the scorecard, a reference for a site outside the US.
monitor: Tydal: letters of credit ($1.3bn anticipated) and first 66.5 gross MW (about 60.5 IT) in 4Q26.
Project debt or ATM for about $500mn Tydal capex remaining.
Related-party funding: BIT facilities $423.3mn at 29 September, some at one-week tenor.
name: Bitdeer

questions.question: Tydal's first 66.5 gross MW is due this quarter and the $1.3bn of letters of credit were 'anticipated' in August. Has J.P. Morgan's LC been issued, who is the second bank, and what happens to the lease and your $500mn of remaining capex if they are not?

You filed a $1bn ATM in August and announced a $100mn buyback in October with the stock near $7. You sold $58.0mn net through 29 September. How much since, at what price, and what share of 2027 capex is equity?
questions.why: Tests non-dilutive claim and per-share value.

questions.question: BIT related-party facilities reached $423.3mn at 29 September, including one-week money. What is the maturity profile and what is the rollover plan?
The tenant can exit at year 10 on a 16-year lease. What does a project lender count, and what rent do you assume for years 11 to 16?
Backlog tripled to $2.9bn on ARR of about $86mn. When does A102, now moved to 1Q27, start, and what GPU cost and prepayment back A201 at over $1.7bn?
questions.why: Tests AI Cloud conversion and owned-GPU risk.

sections.body: Engine: mines bitcoin on its own SEALMINER rigs and converts owned power into AI colocation and GPU cloud, funded by ATM equity, converts, related-party loans and planned project debt. Revenue map: 2Q self-mining about 74%, AI Cloud about 6% (our calc); Tydal about $294mn a year average ($4.7bn / 16, our calc). Costs: power $44/MWh; R&D $36.1mn; G&A $34.3mn. Sensitivities: BTC and hash price, ARR and utilization, ATM price. What would break it, as filed: Volta LC or milestones, capital and dilution, hash price, Tydal delays, Clarington suit; short-tenor rollover is our addition.
